records.name: Sarah Kemp
records.bio: Kemp authored the 2012 finding aid for the Academy of Natural Sciences of Philadelphia’s Blaschka glass models. That record preserves collection extent, historical counts, original components, condition problems, provenance and the 2012 rehousing and display history.

records.name: Geoffrey N. Swinney
records.roles: museum curator · National Museums Scotland collection historian
records.bio: Swinney reconstructed the history of the Blaschka models in National Museums Scotland, including the large nineteenth-century acquisitions and institutional succession of the collection. His study is the principal published anchor for the Edinburgh group.

records.name: Thomas C. Archer
records.bio: Archer directed the Edinburgh Museum of Science and Art through the 1866 and 1868 Blaschka orders. His record makes the museum’s early acquisition history legible at person level rather than leaving it as an anonymous institutional transaction.

records.name: Sarah E. Parker
records.bio: Parker’s UCL documentation is preserved in the provenance trail for individual Grant Museum Blaschka objects, including the beadlet anemone. Her work is a modern bridge between legacy collection records, teaching history and public object interpretation.

records.name: Marek Janáč
records.bio: Janáč’s 2025 article uses National Museum evidence to reconstruct the history of Prague’s surviving Blaschka octopus, including earlier display with a jellyfish model and the loss of the latter during the 1945 destruction of the museum.

records.name: Armin Laussegger
records.bio: Laussegger co-authored the collections-science report that brought the recently rediscovered Seitenstetten sea-anemone models into a wider history of the abbey’s teaching and natural-history collections. The report also links the models cautiously to Frič’s commercial range.

records.name: Sandra Sam
records.bio: Sam co-authored the 2024 Seitenstetten collections report and leads the current university project studying the abbey’s natural-history cabinet. That work provides the institutional framework for inventory, documentation and conservation of the newly identified Blaschka models.

records.name: Markus Bürscher
records.bio: Bürscher co-authored the 2026 report on the current Seitenstetten collections-science project. The report records the identification of sixty-one Blaschka models and the project’s work on inventory, documentation and conservation planning.

records.name: Theresia Hauenfels
records.bio: Hauenfels co-authored the 2026 report on research at the Seitenstetten collections-science centre. Her record connects the rediscovered Blaschka models with the broader institutional programme of inventory, documentation and conservation.

records.name: Tat'jána Spunarová
records.bio: Spunarová co-authored the major study of Václav Frič and his influence on natural-history collecting. For the Blaschka network, the article is especially important for Frič’s retailing of glass invertebrates and his catalogue-based supply to museums and teaching collections.
